title: Juniper and the Gravity
premise: Elodie Reyes smuggles memories—recorded lives, stolen histories, black-market griefs—between the dying colony of Juniper and the orbital stations that pretend it doesn't exist. When a ship that never flew appears on her manifests carrying a passenger name that shouldn't exist, she uncovers an inheritance scheme: the colony's founding families, in cryosleep aboard a ghost vessel, are being quietly written out of humanity's future by the consortium that abandoned them. As customs closes in and the jump window shrinks, Elodie must choose which half of the sleepers wakes—the founders' heirs, or the colonists' descendants who actually built the world—and she chooses neither, broadcasting every stored memory to both ships, forcing justice outside any law before the window seals forever.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the personal effects of people who died intestate. She writes science fiction about paper trails, inheritance, and the bureaucratic violence of forgetting.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Living
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A routine run: Elodie slips a widow's recorded memories past orbital customs inside a shipment of seed grain. We learn Juniper's slow death through what people pay to remember. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Reconciling ledgers, she finds the Meridian listed as flown and paid—yet it never launched. One passenger name repeats across three falsified manifests: V. Okafor-Reyes. Her own surname. Beat: unease.

chapters.title: What the Dockmaster Knows
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. She bribes dockmaster Sefu for the Meridian's true status; he warns her to stop asking and gives her a physical keychip older than the colony's collapse. Beat: first ally, first threat.

chapters.title: Cryosleep Is a Kind of Debt
chapters.summary: POV Idris, a consortium auditor newly arrived to audit Elodie's route. He notices the same ghost manifest and begins pulling threads from the other direction. Beat: antagonist introduced with sympathy.

chapters.title: The Founders' Vault
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The keychip opens a sealed sub-basement beneath the old charter house: records proving two hundred founding-family members entered cryosleep aboard the Meridian forty years ago—and never launched. Beat: revelation, vertigo.

chapters.title: People Who Paid to Forget
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Tracing memory-sales, she finds colonists were paid in rations to surrender recordings of the boarding night—someone erased the launch from collective memory. Beat: horror at complicity.

chapters.title: Auditor
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Idris confronts Elodie under cover of a customs inspection; each realizes the other knows. Uneasy truce over bad coffee. Beat: cat-and-mouse becomes wary partnership.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The Meridian's cryo-banks hold two populations: founding heirs with legal claims, and indentured colonists loaded later as 'ballast.' Only half can wake before life support fails. Beat: the moral engine ignites.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Flashback-adjacent: Idris discovers his own employer authored the abandonment order, and that his audit is meant to bury it, not expose it. Beat: loyalty fractures.

chapters.title: Sefu's Price
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Consortium enforcers arrive hunting the leak; Sefu covers Elodie's escape but is detained. Guilt hardens into resolve. Beat: cost of curiosity made flesh.

chapters.title: Memories Are Contraband
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie raids her own smuggled inventory for the erased boarding-night recordings, bartering with black-market contacts to reassemble the truth. Beat: her criminal skill becomes the colony's only archive.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Idris locates V. Okafor-Reyes—a living heir, awake all along, who has been quietly signing away the sleepers' claims for consortium stipends. Betrayal inside the betrayal. Beat: the name on the manifest explained.

chapters.title: Window Math
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Hard numbers: the jump window closes in eleven days; waking everyone kills them; waking half dooms the rest to drift. Elodie refuses both options and starts planning something illegal even by her standards. Beat: decision point.

chapters.title: Broadcast Rights
chapters.summary: POV Elodie and Idris alternating. Plan forms: use the colony's dead relay array to broadcast every stored memory—open-source, unownable—to both ships and the inner system. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Customs Raid
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Enforcers hit her safehouse; she escapes through the seed-grain routes of chapter one, losing most of her inventory but keeping the core archive. Beat: pursuit, sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Idris Signs
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Ordered to certify the abandonment as routine, Idris instead certifies the Meridian as 'active'—a forgery that legally prevents the consortium from scuttling it. Beat: the auditor commits his first crime.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Climbing the dead array in a storm of solar weather, Elodie and Sefu's daughter begin the upload. Power fails at sixty percent. Beat: climax begins, bodies against machinery.

chapters.title: Everything Everyone Remembered
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief voices. The broadcast completes: the boarding night, the abandonment order, the ballast lists, live to both ships and every station. The consortium's version of history dies publicly. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Idris. With the truth public, crews on both vessels mutiny against their orders; the consortium cannot scuttle the Meridian without admitting everything. Idris surrenders himself to buy time for the waking sequence. Beat: costly victory.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. They wake everyone anyway—slowly, rotating life support, rationing the window's margin, gambling on the mutinied crews' aid. First sleepers open their eyes to a world that remembers them. Beat: grace after arithmetic.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Weeks later: no court will hear the case, but no one will trade with the consortium either. The awakened colonists and heirs must share one small world or none. Elodie hands over the archive and steps back. Beat: letting go of power.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Gravity
chapters.summary: POV Elodie, final. She takes one last smuggling run—not out, but back down, carrying nothing contraband except a recorded goodbye from Idris in custody. Juniper pulls her home like gravity. Beat: quiet, earned belonging.
